[AP Photo/Farid Abdulwahed] After a pause of five days, American warplanes struck targets again in Iran early Thursday morning local time. The hour-long bombardment, which killed a family of three on Qeshm Island according to Iranian state media, including a 2-year-old child, was framed by Washington as a retaliation for attacks Tuesday and Wednesday by Tehran on US assets in Jordan and Egypt. Speaking like a mafia hitman ahead of the US attack, President Donald Trump stated at the White House Wednesday that the US was “going to beat the f***ing sh** out of Iran.” He added, “We’re going to be hitting them very hard because it’s our turn to hit them. They know it’s coming. They asked us not to do it.” The Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for retaliatory attacks Thursday on military bases in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain where US equipment is located. Washington denied Iranian claims that the attack in Jordan had destroyed three F-35 fighter jets and damaged three more. Whatever the truth of these assertions, the bourgeois-clerical regime in Tehran clearly retains the ability to hit US bases throughout the region. It also retains control over the crucial Strait of Hormuz, which accounted for about one-fifth of the world’s oil tanker traffic prior to the war. Trump ordered a pause to 13 nights of US air strikes on Iranian targets Friday under conditions in which US munition stockpiles, especially for its missile defence systems, are running low. However, recent days have underscored that American imperialism and its allies continue to systematically escalate the war. On Saturday, Ukraine struck an Iranian ship in the Caspian Sea for the first time, killing an Iranian sailor and demonstrating how the US/NATO war on Russia and the US/Israeli war on Iran are rapidly converging into a global conflagration. The US strikes on Iran came on the heels of the first publicly announced coordinated attack by Saudi Arabia and the US on Iranian-aligned militias in Iraq. Riyadh’s increasing aggression follows the warning by Yemen’s Houthis earlier this month that they would block the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in the Red Sea, posing a major risk to Saudi energy exports. The Popular Mobilisation Force, which consists of Shia militias that have been integrated into the country’s security forces, reported 20 deaths and over 30 injuries in the strikes. A statement from the group denounced the Saudi-US attacks as a “dangerous escalation, a violation of Iraq’s sovereignty and an attack on its official security institutions.” Available from Mehring Books The struggle against imperialism and for workers’ power in Iran A pamphlet by Keith Jones Hours later, an American-owned vessel storing liquified natural gas at the Egyptian port of Damietta was struck by a drone. Iran has yet to publicly claim responsibility for the incident, but Trump placed the blame on Tehran during his White House remarks. It was the first time that targets in Egypt were struck since the US and Israel launched their illegal war in February. The Trump administration is also working to draw the European imperialist powers into the war. According to a Politico report, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth held consultations with his British counterpart Wes Streeting and other senior officials from both governments last Friday on creating a “defensive” patrol mission involving the European powers in the Strait of Hormuz. The mission would be US-led, with some ships tasked with guarding civilian vessels and others deployed to clear mines, the Politico report noted. Streeting and Hegseth held talks with French Armed Forces Minister Catherine Vautrin on the proposal Monday and will continue discussions with other European capitals this week. According to the news site, European officials indicated their reluctance to “jump into a dangerous” mission after Trump failed to consult them prior to launching the war on Iran. The European imperialists’ objections have nothing to do with opposition to military violence. Over the past year and a half, they have emerged as the leading proponents and funders of the aggressive war on Russia, financing and supplying long-range weaponry that Ukraine has used to strike targets far behind the front lines in Russia. Led by Germany, European governments are spending well over a trillion euros to rearm and militarise society on a scale not seen since World War II. Berlin, Paris, and London were above all troubled by the prospect that Trump’s war on Iran could hamper the war on Russia by draining US weaponry and diverting Washington’s attention from the drive to inflict a defeat on Russia in order to subordinate it to a semi-colonial status. Saturday’s missile strike by Ukraine in the Caspian Sea has linked the two fronts in the rapidly intensifying world war more directly than ever before. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky visited the White House just days later for consultations with Trump, the same day that the US President sat down in the Oval Office with the war criminal Benjamin Netanyahu. The genocidal regime in Israel that Netanyahu heads has waged the war on Iran alongside Washington, while at the same time continuing its bloody onslaught on southern Lebanon, the illegal seizure of land from Palestinians in the West Bank and regular strikes on Gaza, where the genocide against the Palestinians continues. The events over recent days fully vindicate the assessment of the US/Israeli war on Iran made by the World Socialist Web Site . In its first statement on the war , issued just hours after Trump launched the war without any democratic consultation in the dead of night, the WSWS noted that in retrospect, the 28 February assault would be compared with Hitler’s 1 September, 1939 invasion of Poland, a criminal act that marked the outbreak of World War II. WSWS International Editorial Board chairman David North continued, He [Trump] has set the United States and the entire world on a disastrous course. This war will not solve the internal social crisis of American society, nor will it reverse the protracted deterioration in the global position of US capitalism. All these contradictions, domestic and international, will be intensified. The war itself will inevitably escalate and engulf the entire planet. How have past regional conflicts in the Middle East eventually pulled in outside powers and escalated into wider wars — is there a historical pattern here? Ask more questions at SocialismAI.com Less than six months on, the war has already engulfed the entire Middle East and is merging with the war on Russia into a zone of conflict embracing much of the Eurasian landmass. NATO’s war on Russia is escalating no less dangerously than the war on Iran in the Middle East. NATO responded aggressively Thursday to the announcement that a missile had crossed into Polish territory in the early hours of the morning, where it crashed in an uninhabited area and left a 10-metre-wide crater. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated that Warsaw was “ready to shoot down the missile if it continued its flight. Everything indicates that it was a Russian KH-101 cruise missile.” Russia was attacking targets in Ukraine at the time, including areas near the border city of Lviv. Eight people were reported killed across Ukraine, while the missile caused no casualties or damage to buildings in Poland. NATO’s Supreme Command confirmed that it had activated its air defence systems alongside Poland. European Union Council President Antonio Costa denounced “Russian aggression,” which he declared to be “a threat to the security of Europe as a whole.” These howls of outrage are thoroughly hypocritical because the NATO powers are to all intents and purposes at war with Russia. Over recent months, the far-right regime in Kiev has launched numerous attacks with long-range drones and missiles paid for by billions of euros in additional funding from the European imperialists on targets throughout Russia, including oil refineries and residential buildings. Numerous workers have died over recent weeks in strikes targeting the warehouses of the retailer Wildberries. Portraying the war as driven by “Russian aggression” against Ukraine’s fight for “democracy” has served the ruling classes in all of the NATO powers as a means to cover up what has from the outset been a predatory war waged to lay hold of natural resources and cheap labour, and secure geostrategic influence. Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine was a reactionary response by Putin’s capitalist-restorationist regime in Moscow, but it followed three decades of NATO’s eastward expansion and the Western-backed coup in Kiev in 2014 aimed at bringing Ukraine under the direct control of the imperialist powers. The same imperialist goals are at play in the Middle East. The contradictions of the capitalist system, between globalised production and the division of the world into nation-states, and between the mass, social character of production and private ownership, are deepening the antagonisms between the major powers and fuelling world war. Stopping this descent into barbarism depends upon the political mobilisation of the international working class on the programme of world socialist revolution to put an end to imperialist war and its root cause: the capitalist profit system. https://www.politico.eu/article/andy-bur.text: LONDON — British Prime Minister Andy Burnham insisted on Tuesday he handled a message back-and-forth with someone impersonating Donald Trump’s chief of staff in the “right way.” He told broadcasters he is not embarrassed by the incident, reiterating that “nothing of consequence” was discussed. POLITICO first reported Monday that the U.K. prime minister had engaged with messages from somebody pretending to be Susie Wiles, a top adviser to the U.S. president. The key aide has previously been the victim of a phone hack, although the White House said the two incidents were not connected. Advertisement Advertisement “All politicians are, you know, receiving these pressures and these challenges, but I did everything right,” Burnham said during a visit to Wolverhampton. “There was a minimal exchange of information of zero consequence, and it was quickly reported,” he added. “I realized that this needed to be reported, and I did so. So I handled it in the right way,” he also said. The incident has raised questions about potential national security vulnerabilities when it comes to the communications of senior politicians. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting was among three Cabinet ministers whose numbers were found online by POLITICO on Monday. Liberal Democrat MP James MacCleary on Tuesday called for an inquiry into the Burnham message exchange, which he described as a “dangerous security breach.” In a letter to the chair of the Intelligence and Security Committee, he wrote: “This is an unacceptable breach. The security of the Prime Ministers’ communications ought to be absolute priority — and yet it appears, in this case, that routine measures to guard against these kinds of breaches were not followed.” Burnham would not say whether the government planned to change procedures in response to the dupe, but insisted that “the correct action has been taken here and in the U.S.” Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art.text: Image source, Inpho Image caption, The top table remained empty at the appointed time By Kevin Sharkey BBC News in Debrecen Published 4 hours ago The Republic of Ireland will now hold their delayed news conference at 14:30 BST before they face Israel in tomorrow's Nations League fixture in Hungary - a fixture campaigners have called on them to boycott. Heimir Hallgrimsson's team are scheduled to meet Israel in Debrecen at 19:45 BST, with the return fixture in Backa Topola, Serbia on 4 October. They have faced calls to withdraw from the games because of the ongoing Israel-Gaza war with a "Stop The Game" campaign - organised by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine - gathering pace. Former Republic of Ireland manager Brian Kerr and ex-international James McClean are among those to have backed calls for a boycott. However, there are also Irish supporters, perhaps less vocal, who have always believed that the match should be played with supporters in attendance. Following Thursday's 1-0 defeat by Kosovo, midfielder Jason Knight opined he didn't think "the game should be going ahead" , while winger Chiedozie Ogbene urged the public to not "put the pressure on us" regarding their approach to the scheduled game. Hallgrimsson and a player were scheduled to meet the media at 09:15 BST (10.15 local time), before training, but the conference was delayed shortly beforehand. A Uefa official entered the room to inform waiting media teams that the press conference was postponed until after training, which would have been about 11:30 BST (12.30 local time). But shortly afterwards, the Uefa official returned to the media room to announce that the Republic of Ireland's training session had also been postponed. Players were locked in a meeting at the team hotel with unconfirmed reports goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu had withdrawn from the fixture with several others considering their positions. However, just around 13:00 BST, the players began to emerge from their meeting room with it soon confirmed they would travel back to the stadium for the planned news conference with training scheduled for 14:45 BST. Image source, Kevin Sharkey Image caption, Reporters have now gathered out side the Republic of Ireland team hotel The fixture has been embroiled in controversy since the two teams were drawn to play each other in Group B3. A team meeting took place on Friday for players to air their views on Sunday's game and the return fixture in Serbia. The players were expected to release a statement at Saturday's news conference, but the delay has added further uncertainty, with some reports of at least one player wishing to withdraw from the squad. It has since emerged the news conference, scheduled to take place at the stadium, is now set to be staged at the team hotel, with Uefa unable to provide information regarding the delay. The armed Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages. In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive in Gaza, during which more than 73,000 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
